dimensions.assessment: Affects depository institution holding companies, insured depository institutions submitting merger or acquisition applications, and federal regulatory agencies.
dimensions.evidence: the Board shall grant or deny an application submitted under this section not later than 90 days after the date on which the application was initially submitted

dimensions.assessment: Significantly alters agency review procedures by imposing mandatory deadlines and automatically approving applications if agencies fail to act.
dimensions.evidence: if the Board does not grant or deny an application within the time period described under clause (i), such application shall be deemed to have been granted.

dimensions.assessment: Imposes procedural and administrative changes on regulatory agencies without direct federal spending or revenue appropriations.
Amends the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, the Home Owners' Loan Act, and the Federal Deposit Insurance Act.
dimensions.evidence: Section 3(b)(1) of the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956 (12 U.S.C. 1842(b)(1)) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent change to federal regulatory review procedures and statutory deadlines for bank acquisitions and mergers.
dimensions.evidence: Section 3(b)(1) of the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956 (12 U.S.C. 1842(b)(1)) is amended

missing_information: Exact count of bank merger and acquisition applications handled annually by the agencies.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes strict 30-day and 90-day review timelines for bank holding company, savings and loan holding company, and bank merger applications, restricts third-party information use, and deems applications approved if deadlines are missed.

card.summary: The Main Street Capital Access Act modifies and lessens various banking regulations, adjusts capitalization requirements and asset thresholds for community banks and holding companies, and alters federal bank supervision, merger reviews, and resolution procedures.
